findings.claim: 'Required Practical: Paper Chromatography'; 'For the required practical chromatography question'; question type '4 marks - Required Practical Method' (also L2 [3] and L3 [5])
findings.truth: J258 has no required practicals. It sets eight Practical Activity Groups (PAGs); learners must complete at least eight practicals covering the listed apparatus and techniques. Chromatography sits in the separation/chromatography group and salt preparation in the production-of-salts group.
findings.evidence: spec chapter C8 PAG table (PAG1-PAG8) and the NEA practical science statement; C5.1 outcomes 6-8 tag PAG3, PAG4 and PAG7

findings.claim: 'Explain why fractional distillation rather than simple distillation is used...' typed '3 marks - Explain (HT)'

findings.evidence: specs/ocr/chemistry-b-21c-J258-bold.md C5.1: no bold statement in the whole topic

findings.claim: Flame tests presented under the heading 'Instrumental Methods of Identification', after a sentence introducing instrumental techniques
findings.truth: The spec separates laboratory analysis (flame tests, precipitation reactions, anion tests) from instrumental analysis (emission spectroscopy). Filing flame tests as an instrumental method teaches the wrong classification for the comparison question C5.2 outcome 6 asks for.
findings.evidence: spec C5.2 narrative: 'Laboratory analysis can be used to identify the metal cations... using flame tests' vs 'Instrumental analysis is widely used in research and in industry. Emission spectroscopy...'

findings.claim: Nine broken KaTeX inline delimiters written as backslash-space-bracket, e.g. 'hydrogen ions (\ (H^+\))', 'ammonia (\ (NH_3\))', 'double arrow (\ (\rightleftharpoons\))'
findings.truth: The KaTeX inline delimiter is backslash-bracket with no space. As written the auto-render skips them and the student sees the raw markup instead of the formula. Five occurrences in lesson 2, four in lesson 4.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md key conventions: 'KaTeX auto-render - inline \(...\)'; recount from _raw.json

findings.claim: 'atom economy = relative formula mass of desired product / sum of relative formula masses of all products x 100', repeated in the dfn, the display formula, the worked example, the takeaway, a flashcard and the mark scheme of practice question 5
findings.truth: C6.4 outcome 6 gives the formula as mass of atoms in desired product / TOTAL MASS OF ATOMS IN THE REACTANTS x 100. A student who states the products version loses the formula mark. The two denominators happen to be numerically equal for a balanced equation, so both worked answers (56% and 17.6%) are unchanged; the CaCO3 example now divides by the reactant and the CH4 question now supplies the reactant Mr values (16 + 18 = 34).

findings.claim: 'If time had been measured in minutes, the rate would be 1.0 cm3/min - these are not the same value.'
findings.truth: The worked example gives 20 cm3 in 20 s = 1.0 cm3/s. The same rate per minute is 60 cm3/min, not 1.0 cm3/min. As written, a unit-care warning teaches that the two units give the same number.
findings.evidence: recomputation: 1.0 cm3/s x 60 s/min = 60 cm3/min

findings.claim: $$N_2 + 3H_2 \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3 \quad \Delta H = \text{exothermic}$$
findings.truth: Enthalpy change is a quantity with a sign and a value, so it cannot equal the word 'exothermic'. For the forward Haber reaction the enthalpy change is negative.
findings.evidence: settled convention: exothermic means a negative enthalpy change

findings.truth: No lesson in this unit claims a paper 1 / paper 2 content split, and no lesson asserts a paper structure at all. J258 has Breadth (01 Foundation / 03 Higher) and Depth (02 / 04) papers, each 90 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 50%, and BOTH papers assess all eight chapters. Nothing to fix.

summary: Four lessons, 21 findings plus 6 notes, 58 edits. One HIGH: the atom economy formula divided by the total mass of the PRODUCTS instead of the reactants (spec C6.4 outcome 6) in six places. The rest are tier-wrapper faults in both directions (atom economy and the whole C5.2 instrumental/flame-test section wrongly hidden as Higher only; three Haber wrappers opening below their headings; pH-logarithm, strong/weak acid, colour/precipitate rate and Haber-condition content untagged), AQA required-practical language where this board has PAGs, nine broken KaTeX delimiters, an off-spec mass spectrometry thread where J258 names emission spectroscopy, and a unit-conversion note claiming 1.0 cm3/s equals 1.0 cm3/min. All knowledge check keys, match orders, Rf values, rate calculations, percentage yield, atom economy, titration mean and every chemical equation were recomputed and are correct.
